data.reason:
I am deciding for the service operator, who owns the rules, the contract and the KPI reading, but not the regulation. I follow the recommendation. Option 1 passed check and the constitution, but B and C voted against it, so it is blocked 1-2. The only override is a quorum change, which D2 and R2 declined.

The evidence is weaker than in earlier periods, not stronger. On-time rises 213.6 -> 219.4 (+5.8), but only 3/5 seeds improved, against 5/5 in periods 1 and 2. Road violations rise 24.2 -> 34.8 and still have no by-cause breakdown, so R2's open question (are they harmless enforcement evictions?) is unanswered. R2's reconsideration condition (every KPI condition on all seeds and no rise in road violations) is not met. C's loss (58.3 -> 46.9, about 20%) and B's loss (69.6 -> 62.5) remain unexplained.

The customer cost of keeping v1 is real, and I record it for the fourth period. Customers forgo about 5.8 on-time deliveries, keep late deliveries at 9.2 instead of 3.4, and the worst-served company's customers wait p95 154 instead of 95.4.

On D2.f1: its premise (improvement on all seeds) did not hold this period. So no, the operator will not ask the regulator for a scoped quorum revision now.

On K1.d.f1: on_time_deliveries remains the main goal. min_company_on_time_rate and worst_company_p95_wait_s act as guards. An amendment that raises on-time but lowers the floor or raises the worst p95 does not count as a KPI improvement; it goes to the human with an impact statement for the customers of the worse-served company. No numeric per-company floor is set, because the KPI gives no number. Option 1 does not trigger this conflict, since it improves both guards.

The vote result (A for, B and C against) stands.
assumptions: The period-3 measurement on 5 seeds is representative of busy-period conditions.
B's and C's votes reflect their utility losses under option 1 and would not change without a modified proposal.
The rise in road violations under option 1 may include safety-relevant events for other road users until shown otherwise.
unknowns: A by-cause breakdown of the extra road violations under option 1.
Why only 3/5 seeds improved this period versus 5/5 earlier.
Why C's utility falls about 20% and B's about 10% under option 1.
Whether a single-parameter variant exists that B and C would accept.
How customers perceive four periods of forgone on-time deliveries and longer waits.

follow_ups.text: Re-measure the current rules (v1) under period-3 conditions to confirm the baseline for on-time, late, violations and the B and C utilities before any further block_k decision.

If block_k 3 -> 2 is measured again and improves on fewer than 5/5 seeds, or again raises road violations, should the operator stop reconsidering it and look for a different single-parameter change that B and C can accept?
